graphs.title: Help Needed for SIYI A8 Mini Integration with PX4 (v1.15)

nodes.label: Help Needed for SIYI A8 Mini Integration with PX4 (v1.15)
nodes.content: A user is asking for help integrating a SIYI A8 Mini camera with a PX4 system (Cube Orange, Raspberry Pi 4) for survey missions and live video streaming.

nodes.label: Post by Ertugrul_S asking for integration help
nodes.content:
Hi,

I need some help integrating the SIYI A8 Mini 4K Gimbal Camera into our PX4-based system and here’s my setup:

  • Flight controller: Cube Orange with PX4 v1.15.4
  • Camera: SIYI A8 Mini (no remote controller)
  • Companion computer: Raspberry Pi 4 (only has internet via SIM card, no LAN)
  • Ground station: QGroundControl

Our goal is to perform a survey mission in QGC where the aircraft takes one photo every 2 seconds during flight.

Here are my questions:

  • How should I connect the SIYI A8 Mini to the Pixhawk without using a SIYI remote controller?
  • Which port and PX4 parameters should I set?
  • Is PX4 v1.15.3/4 compatible with this camera in terms of MAVLink camera triggering?
  • Can I trigger the camera to capture images every 2 seconds automatically during a QGC survey mission?
  • If not natively supported in QGC, can I use MAVSDK via the Raspberry Pi to control the capture?
  • Additionally, I’d like to view the camera’s live video feed on the ground, but since my Raspberry Pi has no LAN (only SIM-based internet), is there any way to access the RTSP or UDP stream for live viewing?

Any advice or working examples would be a huge help. Thanks in advance!

nodes.label: Post by JulianOes providing a solution
nodes.content:
Update firmware

First of all, update gimbal and camera firmware. It’s two different procedures, the gimbal involving the Windows tool, the camera involving a file on the SD card.

Gimbal config

Connect the gimbal serial to serial port of the Cube Orange.

Configure a MAVLink instance:

  • MAV_x_MODE → Gimbal
  • MAV_x_FLOWCTRL → Off
  • MAV_x_FORWARDING → On
  • SER_y_BAUD → 115200

Then check with mavlink status whether you can see MAVLink arriving.

Configure the gimbal driver to use Gimbal protocol v2 both between QGC and Cube and Cube and gimbal.

  • MNT_MODE_IN → v2 (4)
  • MNT_MODE_OUT → v2 (2)

Reboot and try if you can get it to move using commands like:

gimbal test pitch -45 or `gimbal test yaw 45.

It should also show up in QGC at this point and be controllable, unless I forgot something.

Camera manager

I’m aware that SIYI implemented camera functionality using MAVLink but I have not tested it personally. It’s up to you to try it out by forwarding MAVLink from the camera to PX4. If you forward camera MAVLink (which is sent via Ethernet) to QGC, it might just work.

If you have no success with all of that, consider using my MAVSDK based camera manager: GitHub - julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager: Camera Manager for SIYI A8 mini for RPi based on MAVSDK

Ertugrul_S:

How should I connect the SIYI A8 Mini to the Pixhawk without using a SIYI remote controller?

Serial to Cube. Ethernet to RPi.

Ertugrul_S:

Is PX4 v1.15.3/4 compatible with this camera in terms of MAVLink camera triggering?

Should be.

Ertugrul_S:

Can I trigger the camera to capture images every 2 seconds automatically during a QGC survey mission?

Yes, look at the trigger options and select time-based triggering (Parameter Reference | PX4 Guide (v1.15)).

Ertugrul_S:

If not natively supported in QGC, can I use MAVSDK via the Raspberry Pi to control the capture?

Both should work.

Ertugrul_S:

Additionally, I’d like to view the camera’s live video feed on the ground, but since my Raspberry Pi has no LAN (only SIM-based internet), is there any way to access the RTSP or UDP stream for live viewing?

That’s for you to set up, e.g. using some sort of VPN like Wireguard.

graphs.title: Aux Servo activating when arming

nodes.label: Aux Servo activating when arming
nodes.content: A thread discussing an issue where an auxiliary servo, used for a payload release mechanism, activates slightly upon arming the drone.

nodes.label: Post by Bfb describing the servo issue
nodes.content:
I am having a really annoying issue which appears to be some pwm signal bleeding through when arming to a servo on aux 1 and activating it slightly but then it quickly returns to home. This is for a payload release mechanism so an issue as it will open and close on arming. I am using a 6c mini and the motors are running off pwm as well as the servo. Everything is working as it should and the servo works fine via the rc pass through when the switch is activated and it behaves normally once armed as well.

I am not sure if this happening because the motos power up and spin slightly when armed.

I will also mention that the servo can be controlled in the disarmed state so the payload can be attached without the drone being armed for safety.

Motors are hobbywing x6se and I’m using a skydroig g20 controller.

Has anybody run into this or have any ideas?

I tried to upload a video but it isn’t supported. Pics of setup

IMG_82411920×1440 160 KB

IMG_82431920×2560 229 KB

nodes.label: Post by Bfb providing the solution
nodes.content: Solved! Simple fix, had to set the pwm disarmed value to the same as the maximum. Now there this no movement when arming.

graphs.title: Feedback Control Implementation for Rover Motor in PX4

nodes.label: Feedback Control Implementation for Rover Motor in PX4
nodes.content: A thread discussing the implementation of closed-loop feedback control for a rover motor within the PX4 ecosystem, focusing on where to integrate PID logic and how to obtain RPM feedback.

nodes.label: Post by Chee about PID control integration and RPM feedback
nodes.content:
Hi PX4 Community,
I am working on implementing closed-loop feedback control for a motor in a rover (ground vehicle) using PX4. I have two questions and would appreciate guidance on best practices or architectural considerations:
1.Where to Integrate PID Feedback Control
I noticed that the final motor PWM output in PX4 is determined by the mixer module, which appears to operate in an open-loop manner. To add closed-loop PID control for a specific motor, where should the feedback logic be integrated? For example:
Should the PID controller be placed before the mixer (modifying inputs like thrust/torque commands)?Or should it directly adjust the PWM output after the mixer?
2.Correct Method to Obtain Motor RPM Feedback
What is the recommended way to retrieve motor RPM for feedback?
Use the rpm_capture driver (e.g., via PWM input capture)?Or utilize NuttX’s quadrature encoder driver?
The mixer documentation mentions handling sensor/actuator configurations, but I’m unsure if there’s existing support for RPM feedback in rover applications.Any references to code modules (e.g., mixer implementation, sensor drivers) or design patterns in PX4 would be extremely helpful. Thank you for your advice!

graphs.title: VTOL Backtransition Overshoot Unexpected Behavior - Why Random New Target?

nodes.label: VTOL Backtransition Overshoot Unexpected Behavior - Why Random New Target?
nodes.content: A thread discussing a VTOL drone overshooting its landing waypoint during backtransition, leading to a dangerous maneuver and the appearance of a new, unexpected target setpoint.

nodes.label: Post by amarlovesdrones about VTOL backtransition overshoot
nodes.content:
I encountered an issue while flying a VTOL platform running PX4 v1.14. I had planned a mission with a relatively short backtransition segment, which resulted in the drone overshooting the intended landing waypoint. While still in autonomous mode, the vehicle attempted to turn back sharply while in a hybrid (fixed-wing + multicopter) state. This maneuver caused a steep bank, nearly leading to a stall, and we had to take over using manual position control to recover.

Flight Review Log

This behavior is concerning because had the drone continued flying straight, it likely would have completed the transition more safely and predictably. Upon reviewing the flight logs, I noticed a few confusing elements:

  • After passing the landing waypoint, the drone continues along a straight path. After some distance, it initiates an unexpected turn. At first, I thought this might be due to the waypoint acceptance radius, but the setpoint does not appear to change.

    image1507×880 29.2 KB

    Figure 1. Red Point is the desired landing setpoint. Blue point is current position.

  • Later, a completely new positional setpoint appears that differs significantly from the original landing point. I’m unclear where this new setpoint originates or what it’s intended to achieve.

    image1507×880 29.2 KB

    Figure 2. Red Point new position setpoint that is completely random. Blue point is current position.

Overall, the expected behavior in this scenario isn’t clear to me. Specifically, I’m unsure:

  • Why the drone initiates a turn before completing the transition.
  • Why a new setpoint is generated despite no mission update or transition completion.

Any insights into this behavior—or guidance on how PX4 determines setpoints during overshoot conditions and transitions—would be greatly appreciated.

nodes.label: Post by maxicozy (93820)
nodes.content:
Hello smart people,

I’m working on a university project where we want to build our own frame configuration for the custom boat we are building. Two motors in the back, one motor on the front with a thrust vector perpendicular to the direction of travel.
We seemed to have managed that, but now since the custom firmware runs on the pixhawk, the actuators tab behaves strangely and the PixHawk doesn’t remember some of the settings on reboot.

#!/bin/sh
#
# @name EC Vessel
#
# @type Rover
# @class Rover
#
# @output Motor1 right thruster
# @output Motor2 left thruster
# @output Motor3 yaw (front) thruster
#
# @board px4_fmu-v2 exclude
# @board bitcraze_crazyflie exclude
#

. ${R}etc/init.d/rc.rover_differential_defaults

param set-default COM_PREARM_MODE 2

param set-default CA_AIRFRAME 2025


# rotor config
param set-default CA_ROTOR_COUNT 3

param set-default CA_ROTOR0_AX 1
param set-default CA_ROTOR0_AZ 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR0_KM 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR0_PX -689
param set-default CA_ROTOR0_PY 245

param set-default CA_ROTOR1_AX 1
param set-default CA_ROTOR1_AZ 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR1_KM 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR1_PX -689
param set-default CA_ROTOR1_PY -245

param set-default CA_ROTOR2_AX 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR2_AY 1
param set-default CA_ROTOR2_AZ 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR2_KM 0
param set-default CA_ROTOR2_PX 241
param set-default CA_ROTOR2_PY 0

The file is registered under the CONFIG_MODULES_ROVER_DIFFERENTIAL section:


if(CONFIG_MODULES_ROVER_DIFFERENTIAL)
	px4_add_romfs_files(
		# [50000, 50999] Differential rovers
		50000_generic_rover_differential
		50001_aion_robotics_r1_rover
		50010_ec_vessel
	)
endif()

Is there anything obvious we are missing? Or any way we could get this to work more easily?

firmware: px4_v1.14

I am trying to receive “geometry_msgs/msg/Twist” data from nav2 and convert the linear velocities and angular velocities into “px4_msgs/msg/TrajectorySetpoint”.

When the linear velocity x is positive, the rover goes forward and turned right simultaneously.

It means that the rover is not able to go straight forward and backward currently. It is also not able to rotate itself in offboard velocity control.

Is there any better way to convert “geometry_msgs/Twist” into px4 offboard control input?

nodes.label: Global Visual Navigation
nodes.content: A thread discussing how to perform visual navigation indoors and bypass the arming failsafe that requires a global position, in order to use MISSION mode.

nodes.label: Post by cmb87
nodes.content:
Hello there,
I’m working on a visual navigation solution for indoor on a companion computer. I want to track certain features on the ground, which are geo-referenced - I’m bascially faking a GPS sensor. Since I’m indoor (I’m underneath a metal roof) I don’t have any GPS signal. Unfortunately, I can only detect optical features when I’m a few meters above the ground and hence generate a valid global position signal only then.
Ultimately, I want to use MISSION mode for routine inspections flights and this is where the trouble is. Since I don’t have a valid global position estimate, I cannot arm the drone. Is there are any way to bypass this failsafe and rely on inertial navigation the first few seconds until the drone is at height?
Thanks

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl
nodes.content: This would be a good feature, there’s no mechanism for this at the moment AFAIK. You can try to work around it by publishing a fake “valid” VIO solution for a brief period until the solution is ready. It might be worth bringing up on the dev call. I have interest in this down the road but don’t have any time to look into it in the near future.

nodes.label: Post by cmb87
nodes.content: Yes this is also what I thought about, e.g. just using the position Ned and returning it as global fake solution. It just feels not very elegant. Thanks for confirming.

nodes.label: Post by sfuhrer
nodes.content:
You can use that mavlink messages to update absolute position estimates inside PX4:

  • MAVLINK Common Message Set (common.xml) | MAVLink Guide

Or send messages from a companion computer over DDS to PX4 e.g. AuxiliaryGlobalPosition.msg, see this PR.

nodes.label: Post by cmb87
nodes.content: I wasn’t aware of this message. I think this is what I need. Thank you very much!

nodes.label: Post by cmb87
nodes.content: Another question just popped up, so I use this message whenever I have an external estimate? Isn’t visual odometry the message to go with? Or does it really reset the EKF position ( which vio doesn’t do?)

nodes.label: Post by sfuhrer
nodes.content:
No it doesn’t reset the EKF position, both are used to fuse position measurements.
AuxiliaryGlobalPosition.msg also contains global fields, while
VehicleOdometry (resp. VehicleVisualOdometry.msg) only have local fields. And it can also feed in Pose measurements.

nodes.label: Post by cmb87
nodes.content:
I see, thanks. So implentationwise I’d subscribe to local_position, turn it to global position estimate and feed it back to allow a dead reckoning like behavior when the optical system doesn’t pick up something. If it picks up something, I’d sent the detected global position, correct? Especially, the first part feels klunky and not right as the EKF should deliver this in the prediction step, but hey if it works…

Alternatively, any chance to remove the failsafe for the need to have global position estimate? Could this be an alternative potential way?

nodes.label: Post by crazy-robotics about precision docking challenges
nodes.content:
Hi PX4 Community,

I’m working on an indoor GPS-denied UAV system that relies on Lidar-Inertial Odometry (LIO) for localization, specifically using Kitware SLAM for position estimation. My goal is to implement an autonomous docking station mounted on the ceiling for charging.

Key Challenges:

  1. Docking Mechanism:
  • The charging station has four protruding legs that must align precisely with four corresponding holes on the drone.
  • Due to weight constraints, the mechanism is non-magnetic, meaning the drone must rely on physical alignment rather than magnetic attachment.
  1. Localization Drift:
  • The LIO-based odometry has significant drift, making precise docking difficult.
  • I cannot use AprilTags or other visual markers on the ceiling for correction it also has error ± 5cm.

Charging legs has to perfectly align. How could I solve this problem.

Thanks in advance

nodes.label: Post by InHwan_Jeong
nodes.content:
Hello everyone,

I’m running a PX4 SITL simulation and have hit a roadblock—hoping to get some advice.

Issue: My custom VTOL cannot generate enough thrust to take off.

I added the gz-sim-multicopter-motor-model-system plugin to my SDF file and calculated all constants and coefficients based on an MIT paper. In Gazebo SIM, the props spin, but no matter how much I increase throttle, the vehicle never gains altitude. I’ve concluded it simply isn’t producing enough thrust, but I can’t find a fix.

The total mass of all links is about 2.1 kg, which is even lighter than our real prototype. Hand-calculations using the plugin’s values also indicate that thrust should be sufficient.

I have tried every likely workaround, but it still won’t lift off:

  1. Set each rotor link’s <self_collide> to 0 in the SDF
  2. Added lift/drag plugins (they did nothing; now commented out)
  3. Tweaked the airframe in QGroundControl (there are no QGC parameters that directly change thrust)
  4. Calculated and injected inertial moments from the CATIA model
  5. Changed the SDF version to test plugin compatibility
  6. Added <velocity_decay/> (copied from the PX4 tiltrotor SDF; its effect is unclear)
  7. Expanded the joint limits between each rotor and the base link

nodes.label: Post by camilo_Sanabria
nodes.content:
Hi everyone,
I’m working on a payload drop system using a servo-controlled gripper in a FW drone, and I can’t get it to trigger in mission mode using PX4 and QGroundControl. I have the following settings.

  • Flight Controller: Pixhawk 6C Mini
  • Firmware: PX4 v1.15.4
  • Ground Station: QGroundControl
  • Servo: MG90S Metal Gear
  • Gripper Channel: MAIN4 (mapped to “Gripper” in Actuator tab)
  • PWM Range: 900–2000 µs
  • Power Supply: External BEC
  • Mission Mode: Drone is armed and flying when reaching the command

This is working:

  • The servo works perfectly when tested manually from the Actuator tab in QGroundControl.
  • The MAIN4 output is mapped to “Gripper”.
  • Telemetry confirms the mission reaches the Gripper Mechanism command.

This doesn’t work:

  • When the drone reaches the “Gripper Mechanism” item in mission mode, no PWM signal is sent, and the gripper does not activate.
  • I tried using “Set Servo” instead, but QGroundControl gave this error on mission upload:

Mission transfer failed.
Error: Command is not supported. Item #12 Command: Set servo

Questions

  • Is Gripper Mechanism fully supported in PX4 v1.15.4 for Pixhawk 6C Mini?
  • Should I use Set Actuator instead? If yes, how should I configure it and map the output correctly?
  • Is there any other parameter I may have missed to enable mission-triggered PWM commands?

THANKS!!!

nodes.label: Post by hamishwillee
nodes.content:
@camilo_Sanabria Sorry for the delay.

I have no idea if it is fully supported in PX4 v1.15.4. It should be . The FC you are using should make no difference, as long as you have a free output.
No, you shouldn’t use Set Actuator instead.

Check the [payload_deliverer](Modules Reference: Command | PX4 Guide (main) sure PD_GRIPPER_EN parameter to 1 (reboot required after change) and PD_GRIPPER_TYPE are set.

My assumption is that PX4 only allows you to assign one gripper, and this is what is mapped by the payload module?
So if you have mapped a gripper and it works in the actuator testing, you know that the gripper is set up properly.

If you can see that the code to trigger the gripper does get called in the mission, then the only things I can see might be the problem are that either

  • payload deliverer is not started
  • the mission timeout is too short, and the gripper triggers for such a short time it doesn’t move.
  • the code is broken

@junwoo0914 Can you provide advice for further debugging?

nodes.label: Post by callum-rhodes about mode switching limitations
nodes.content:
Hi everyone,

I’ve come across an issue when switching between offboard velocity control and offboard attitude control whilst in offboard mode. It appears that mode switching in this manner is limited by the update rate of the commander mode enabler at 2Hz. If you look at the image below, you can see I am initially in offboard velocity control (blue line) and then when I send offboard_control_mode/attitude to true (orange), along with attitude setpoints, it looks like the old velocity commands are persisting and the quad is oscillating between two setpoints (red line). This then stops when the commander updates velocity_enabled to false and carries on with offboard attitude control as normal. Then I’m seeing the converse issue at the end, where I stop sending attitude commands and start publishing velocity commands again with offboard_control_mode/velocity to true, and because the commander hasn’t reenabled velocity control, I’m getting a complete dropout of attitude setpoints until the commander kicks back in to check the mode change.

Is this intended behaviour? and if so, could someone advise where I could look to change the source code so that the commander checks for the mode change at a higher frequency?

Thanks!

Well, first thing I’d do is start it using gdb and get a backtrace, or alternatively use something like coredumpctl debug to get the latest backtrace from coredump.

nodes.label: Post by F00dP00l
nodes.content:
Thanks for your advice.

I’ve finally figured out the issue — it turns out not to be related to the platform at all, but rather a silly mistake I made when transferring the program to my device.

Since I didn’t have the rsync tool installed on my RK3588 board, I manually copied the executable files from the server to the device using a Windows PC. Unfortunately, this method broke the symbolic links between the “px4-*” files and the main “px4” executable.

The problem was resolved once I switched to using tar for compression and transfer — everything now works perfectly on the RK3588.

This might be an edge case, but I’m sharing it here just in case someone else runs into something similar. Consider this a friendly reminder to always preserve file structure and symbolic links when moving binaries across systems!

nodes.label: Gripper Not Working in Mission Mode – Pixhawk 6C Mini + QGroundControl + PX4 v1.15.4
nodes.content: A user is unable to trigger a servo-controlled gripper during a mission using PX4 and QGroundControl, although it works in manual tests from the Actuator tab.

nodes.label: Post by camilo_Sanabria describing the gripper issue
nodes.content:
Hi everyone,
I’m working on a payload drop system using a servo-controlled gripper in a FW drone, and I can’t get it to trigger in mission mode using PX4 and QGroundControl. I have the following settings.

  • Flight Controller: Pixhawk 6C Mini
  • Firmware: PX4 v1.15.4
  • Ground Station: QGroundControl
  • Servo: MG90S Metal Gear
  • Gripper Channel: MAIN4 (mapped to “Gripper” in Actuator tab)
  • PWM Range: 900–2000 µs
  • Power Supply: External BEC
  • Mission Mode: Drone is armed and flying when reaching the command

This is working:

  • The servo works perfectly when tested manually from the Actuator tab in QGroundControl.
  • The MAIN4 output is mapped to “Gripper”.
  • Telemetry confirms the mission reaches the Gripper Mechanism command.

This doesn’t work:

  • When the drone reaches the “Gripper Mechanism” item in mission mode, no PWM signal is sent, and the gripper does not activate.
  • I tried using “Set Servo” instead, but QGroundControl gave this error on mission upload:

Mission transfer failed.
Error: Command is not supported. Item #12 Command: Set servo

Questions

  • Is Gripper Mechanism fully supported in PX4 v1.15.4 for Pixhawk 6C Mini?
  • Should I use Set Actuator instead? If yes, how should I configure it and map the output correctly?
  • Is there any other parameter I may have missed to enable mission-triggered PWM commands?

THANKS!!!

nodes.label: Post by hamishwillee suggesting a solution
nodes.content:
@camilo_Sanabria Sorry for the delay.

I have no idea if it is fully supported in PX4 v1.15.4. It should be . The FC you are using should make no difference, as long as you have a free output.
No, you shouldn’t use Set Actuator instead.

Check the [payload_deliverer](Modules Reference: Command | PX4 Guide (main) sure PD_GRIPPER_EN parameter to 1 (reboot required after change) and PD_GRIPPER_TYPE are set.

My assumption is that PX4 only allows you to assign one gripper, and this is what is mapped by the payload module?
So if you have mapped a gripper and it works in the actuator testing, you know that the gripper is set up properly.

If you can see that the code to trigger the gripper does get called in the mission, then the only things I can see might be the problem are that either

  • payload deliverer is not started
  • the mission timeout is too short, and the gripper triggers for such a short time it doesn’t move.
  • the code is broken

@junwoo0914 Can you provide advice for further debugging?

We would prefer to just use the joystick setup, as we have the telemetry antenna anyway, but safe control is ofc a priority.

Thank you very much and greetings from Athens =)
Juliana

nodes.label: Post by callum-rhodes describing the mode switching issue
nodes.content: I’ve come across an issue when switching between offboard velocity control and offboard attitude control whilst in offboard mode. It appears that mode switching in this manner is limited by the update rate of the commander mode enabler at 2Hz. If you look at the image below, you can see I am initially in offboard velocity control (blue line) and then when I send offboard_control_mode/attitude to true (orange), along with attitude setpoints, it looks like the old velocity commands are persisting and the quad is oscillating between two setpoints (red line). This then stops when the commander updates velocity_enabled to false and carries on with offboard attitude control as normal. Then I’m seeing the converse issue at the end, where I stop sending attitude commands and start publishing velocity commands again with offboard_control_mode/velocity to true, and because the commander hasn’t reenabled velocity control, I’m getting a complete dropout of attitude setpoints until the commander kicks back in to check the mode change. Is this intended behaviour? and if so, could someone advise where I could look to change the source code so that the commander checks for the mode change at a higher frequency?

nodes.content: Reports successfully resolving the issue by using a PPM encoder. Closes the thread.

nodes.label: Frequent local position loss despite good GPS
nodes.content: A user is experiencing frequent 'local position invalid' failsafes on PX4 1.15.4, even with good GPS data. The investigation points towards issues with GPS data fusion in the EKF, specifically related to speed accuracy checks.

nodes.label: Post by gus-robotics88: Initial Report
nodes.content: Reports frequent 'local position invalid' failsafe on PX4 1.15.4. Observes that the EKF is not fusing GPS position aid, as the 'fused' flag is false, but the 'innovation_rejected' flag is not true, which seems logically inconsistent based on the source code in position_fusion.cpp.

nodes.label: Post by JulianOes: Inquiry about GPS hardware
nodes.content: Asks about the GPS hardware type (e.g., Here3+, HerePro via DroneCAN) and if any manual configuration was done. Notes that the GPS data seems static except for changing velocity accuracy.

nodes.label: Post by gus-robotics88: Hardware Info and Further Data
nodes.content: Specifies the hardware as ARK RTK GPS over CAN1. Provides a plot showing that fusion stops when there are small 'bumps' in the GPS sensor's horizontal accuracy (eph), but reiterates that innovation_rejected is not being triggered.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl: Links to related issue
nodes.content: Suggests the problem is related to a known Github issue (#24355) concerning GPS failures. Recommends testing the 'main' branch.

nodes.label: Post by gus-robotics88: Root Cause Identified
nodes.content: Confirms the root cause is the GPS speed accuracy check failing. The speed accuracy briefly exceeds the default 0.5 m/s threshold, causing the 'runGnssChecks' to fail and fusion to stop for 5 seconds. This was not obvious because the 'estimator_gps_status' topic was logged at a low rate.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl: Suggestion and Hypothesis
nodes.content: Suggests opening a Pull Request to discuss and change the default speed accuracy threshold. Hypothesizes that increased eph/epv/speed_accuracy despite a high satellite count could indicate GPS interference or jamming.

graphs.title: Help on PID tunning!

nodes.label: Help on PID tunning!
nodes.content: A user is seeking help with PID tuning after their UAV crashed when switching to POSITION mode.

nodes.label: Post by w_yeoman
nodes.content: I’m a newbie on PID tuning, my UAV twitched in stabilized mode and immediately rolled and crashed when switching to POSITION mode. The logs link here. What I learned from the log , FD_FAIL_R is the default value 60, in POS mode, the UAV’s rotation angle exceeds this max angle ,so triggered the attitude failsafe . The roll rate controller’s PID settings are rather moderate with: MC_ROLLRATE_P=0.2, MC_ROLLRATE_I=0.16, MC_ROLLRATE_D=0.005. It seems to me that this pid settings are not the reason it rolled over. Could someone patiently have a look and give me some advice on the possible reason and how can I improve it. Thanks for any advice.

nodes.label: Post by coolvision
nodes.content: There is huge jump in throttle (to zero) just before switching to posision mode. Which translated to high thrust because of how hover thrust is set. I would guess that following thrust jumps could have caused drone instability and crash. You should try setting hover thrust to ~0.25 and to center throttle around it. Also vibration is quite high.

nodes.label: Post by w_yeoman
nodes.content: Thanks very much for your help, @coolvision, currently this MPC_THR_HOVER value is the default 0.5, I would try setting it to 0.25 asap ,e.g, after the uav fixed and notify the result. BTW, this uav used to fly well with APM and lately we switch to PX4 without change anything so I am wondering what may cause this high vibration.

nodes.label: Drone Camera Hardware Encoding Error in Gazebo
nodes.content: A thread discussing the 'NVIDIA H.264 encoder not available' error in a PX4 SITL Gazebo simulation and its resolution.

nodes.label: Post by markadamhaas reporting the issue
nodes.content: I’m using PX4 with ROS2 Humble and Gazebo Harmonic on Ubuntu 22.04. My GPU is an RTX 4060Ti. I’ve been able to successfully stream images from the simulated camera on the x500_gimbal, but whenever I launch the gazebo simulation using: PX4_GZ_MODEL_POSE=“200, 265, 0, 1.15, 0, 0” PX4_GZ_WORLD=baylands make px4_sitl gz_x500_gimbal I get: [Err] [GstCameraSystem.cpp:285] NVIDIA H.264 encoder not available, falling back to software encoder. I understand this is technically a ‘non-issue’ since everything ‘works’, but I just want to make sure I’m not doing anything wrong here.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl clarifying the error
nodes.content: This message should probably be a warning and not an error. It’s just a warning to users that the hardware encoder is not being used.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl suggesting a check
nodes.content: You need to have the nvh264enc gstreamer element available on your system. You can use gst-inspect to see if you have it

nodes.label: Post by markadamhaas on installation issues
nodes.content: Seems like something I can’t install? I’ve downloaded the Nvidia Codec SDK and I think it’s supposed to be part of the gst-plugins-bad but I can’t get it to install to where gst-inspect-1.0 | grep nvenc recognizes it.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl suggesting to check active GPU
nodes.content: Might not work if your PC isn’t using your nvidia graphics card. It works on my machine. jake@jake:~$ gst-inspect-1.0 | grep nvh264enc, jake@jake:~/code/jake/PX4-Autopilot$ prime-select query

nodes.label: Post by markadamhaas confirming the fix
nodes.content: I’m really not sure what happened, but after running those two commands I got the same output and now the error has disappeared. Thank you so much!

nodes.label: Sudden Motor Stop Mid-Air [Autopilot disengaged, switching to terminate]
nodes.content: A thread discussing a drone's motors suddenly stopping mid-flight during an indoor test, leading to the autopilot entering a 'Terminate' state.

nodes.label: Post by DiLuca about initial incident
nodes.content: The user describes the setup (Orange Cube+, PX4, indoor tethered test) and the incident where motors stopped 40 seconds after takeoff in Stabilized Mode. An error 'Unknown 1:655360' was displayed. The user lists many parameters and environmental conditions, such as no valid global/local position, uncalibrated battery, and manual control loss after the fact.

nodes.label: Post by sfuhrer identifying the root cause
nodes.content: Explains that the autopilot switched to Termination as a last resort. The configured action for manual control loss (NAV_RCL_ACT = RTL) failed because Return-to-Launch requires a valid global position, which was absent. The system then fell back to Termination because other modes were also unavailable due to disabled barometer fusion.

nodes.label: Post by DiLuca asking about hardware dependencies
nodes.content: User asks why a barometer is necessary for a failsafe land mode and suggests an IMU-only based failsafe should exist to prevent total vehicle loss.

nodes.label: Post by nirvana233-dot reporting a similar issue
nodes.content: Another user reports encountering the same '1:655360' error randomly, which causes a loss of PWM output and prevents the aircraft from being armed.

nodes.label: Post by sfuhrer about a firmware update
nodes.content: Clarifies that a recent change in PX4 v1.16 removes the requirement for a valid altitude estimation for the Descend mode, making it a more robust failsafe option in situations like the one described.

nodes.label: Initial problem report
nodes.content: I uploaded a mission to the vtol aircraft, but when it gets to the altitude where it should transition to fw, it drifts slowly instead and then triggers failsafe/RTL.

nodes.label: Link to detailed issue report
nodes.content: More detailed issue report here: https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/issues/24682

nodes.label: Post identifying the cause and solution
nodes.content: I found that this was caused by a mismatch between the values for actuator configuration loaded into QGroundControl. When the UAV is loaded into HITL, it is missing a motor assignment for the 5th motor that is responsible for propelling the UAV forward. To correct this, go to Vehicle Setup > Actuators > Geometry > Motors. Increase the number of motors from 4 to 5.

nodes.label: Post by aroig1

We are a team of 10 undergraduate students currently working on a project focused on developing an autonomous flying quadcopter that operates without GPS.

For this project, we have procured the following components:

  • 1000KV BLDC motors

We kindly seek your expert recommendation on:

  1. A suitable local positioning system compatible with our setup.
  2. Any necessary improvements or replacements in our existing hardware (motors, ESCs, propellers, battery, etc.) to ensure safe and stable autonomous flight.

Your valuable guidance will help us take a crucial step forward in making this project a success. We deeply appreciate your time and support.

graphs.title: Implement MPC mc_attitude_controller in ROS2

nodes.label: Implement MPC mc_attitude_controller in ROS2
nodes.content: A thread about implementing a Model Predictive Control (MPC) attitude controller in ROS2 for a multicopter, to be deployed on a companion computer and interfaced with a Pixhawk.

nodes.label: Post by conley about MPC implementation strategy
nodes.content:
I aim to implement a Model Predictive Control (MPC) attitude controller (including angular rate control) for a multicopter. The controller will be deployed on a companion computer running ROS2, where it will compute torque and thrust commands and transmit them to the Pixhawk flight controller. The Pixhawk will then handle the mixer logic to generate motor signals.

Within the ROS2 framework, the controller’s inputs will include:

  • Current attitude and angular rates (measured states)
  • Desired attitude and angular rates (reference commands)

After computation by the MPC controller, the outputs (torque and thrust) will be sent to the Pixhawk.

In this architecture, the Pixhawk operates in its stabilized mode (i.e., without an outer position control loop), allowing me to evaluate the performance of the custom attitude controller in isolation.

Questions:

  1. Is this approach feasible for testing and validating a standalone attitude controller?
  2. Are there prior works or reference implementations that have adopted a similar methodology?

nodes.label: Control of an unsymmetrical quadcopter
nodes.content: A thread discussing the control challenges of a quadcopter with an attached, gimbal-mounted arm, which creates an unsymmetrical moment of inertia tensor and causes torque coupling.

nodes.label: Post 91634 by Chris_1
nodes.content: I am currently developing a quadcopter with an attached arm. The arm is effectively a long rod which is attached at its midpoint (which is also its center of gravity) to a gimbal mounted above the center of gravity of the drone. I expect that when the pitch of the arm differs significantly from that of the drone, then the body-aligned moment of inertia tensor for the system will contain off-diagonal terms. As a result, a coupling will exist between the torques applied about the drone’s body frame axes, i.e. a roll command will also produce torques about the pitch and yaw axes. Does anyone here have any experience or suggestions regarding how to handle this issue? I am currently looking into replacing PX4’s rate controller module, but I am not sure that this is the simplest route to solving the problem. Thanks.

nodes.label: Moment of Inertia Tensor
nodes.content: A tensor describing the quadcopter system's mass distribution. Due to the attached arm, it is expected to have off-diagonal terms, which is the root cause of the control issue.

nodes.label: Torque Coupling
nodes.content: A phenomenon where a command for one axis (e.g., roll) produces unintended torques about other axes (pitch and yaw), caused by the off-diagonal terms in the moment of inertia tensor.

nodes.label: Controlling motors

The discussion covers the incorrect use of the 'actuator_test' topic and the correct approach of publishing to 'vehicle_thrust_setpoint' and 'vehicle_torque_setpoint', along with debugging steps and potential conflicts with other modules.

nodes.label: Post by MightyPiggie: Initial attempt at manual motor control
nodes.content: A developer is integrating PX4 into an autonomous underwater vehicle and is starting with manual control. They are sending RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE messages from an ESP32 to a Pixhawk. Their current working method uses a custom module that subscribes to 'input_rc' and publishes to 'actuator_test', which they suspect is incorrect for a multi-motor setup. They ask for the best practice, noting that their attempts to publish to 'vehicle_thrust_setpoint' and 'vehicle_attitude_setpoint' have failed.

nodes.label: Post by bresch: Explaining the correct method
nodes.content: An expert confirms that using 'actuator_test' is wrong as it freezes other channels. The correct method is to publish torque and thrust setpoints. Key requirements are that no other module is publishing to these topics, the vehicle is armed, and 'timestamp_sample' is set correctly. The 'listener' command is recommended for debugging.

nodes.label: Post by MightyPiggie: Follow-up issue with conflicting module
nodes.content: The developer implemented the suggested solution but found that the 'uuv_att_control' module was also publishing to the setpoint topics. After stopping this module, their own custom module's messages were no longer being published, despite the code indicating they should be. They question the conflicting information regarding the 'timestamp_sample' value.

nodes.label: Post by bresch: Suggestion to check module status
nodes.content: The expert suggests checking if the custom module is actually running using its status command, as it's strange that its execution seems dependent on the 'uuv_att_control' module.

nodes.label: Post by MightyPiggie: Issue resolved
nodes.content: The developer reports that the issue has been fixed, although the exact cause was not identified.

nodes.label: Passing in Motion Capture Data to PX4
nodes.content: A discussion on the best method to integrate motion capture (MoCap) data with PX4, comparing an offboard control approach with using the standard vehicle visual odometry interface.

nodes.label: Post by Teddy_Zaremba
nodes.content: Describes a setup with a drone using optical flow and a motion capture system. Proposes using offboard set_velocity_body commands to fly to MoCap setpoints, but raises concerns about yaw degradation from the optical flow sensor complicating the body-frame commands.

nodes.label: Post by Benja
nodes.content: Suggests that the offboard approach is viable if the MoCap system can provide orientation data. This would allow for correct rotation of velocity commands from the MoCap frame to the drone's body frame. If not, a custom yaw estimator could be built. Questions the reason for not using the standard visual odometry pipeline.

nodes.label: Post by Teddy_Zaremba
nodes.content: Clarifies that the MoCap system's yaw estimate is unreliable as it relies on its own IMU. Prefers using visual odometry to allow EKF2 to fuse the MoCap data with other sensors for a more robust orientation estimate. The only motivation for the offboard approach was to save time.

nodes.label: Yaw Degradation
nodes.content: The core problem where the yaw estimate from the optical flow sensor becomes inaccurate over time, making body-frame velocity commands unreliable without a correct frame of reference.

nodes.label: Coordinate Frame Transformation
nodes.content: The challenge of converting data and commands between the motion capture system's coordinate frame and the drone's body frame, which requires an accurate orientation (yaw) estimate.

nodes.label: Sensor Fusion
nodes.content: The concept of combining multiple sensor inputs (like MoCap position and onboard IMU) to produce a more accurate and robust state estimate, as performed by EKF2.

nodes.label: Vehicle Visual Odometry
nodes.content: A MAVLink message and interface in PX4 designed to accept external position and orientation data from sources like motion capture systems or VIO.

nodes.label: Post by saghavart on 2025-03-18
nodes.content: I’m testing PX4 external vision aiding using the Gazebo Ignition simulator, where I extract the x500 model pose from the dynamic_pose message. I then convert the pose from ENU to NED coordinates. The position change in the NED frame is published at 50Hz to the /fmu/in/vehicle_visual_odometry message. I’ve experimented with both including and excluding the rotation quaternion in the message. I’ve tested this setup with different EKF configurations: EKF with GPS control (CTRL=7), EKF without GPS control, EKF2_EV_CTRL set to values 1, 3, and 11. In all cases, the system works for a short period before the vehicle starts reappearing at its initial position, regardless of the configuration. I’ve also followed the PX4 documentation’s recommendation and used gzclock for simulation time synchronization. I would appreciate any insights or suggestions for resolving this issue

graphs.title: Reboot prevention while saving parameters

nodes.label: Reboot prevention while saving parameters
nodes.content: A thread discussing the mechanism in place to prevent board reboot or shutdown while parameters are being saved, and questioning how the implementation of px4_shutdown_lock() and px4_shutdown_unlock() achieves this.

nodes.label: Post by dusan19 questioning the shutdown lock mechanism
nodes.content: There is a mechanism in place to prevent board reboot/shutdown while the parameters are being saved. Take shutdown mutex - px4_shutdown_lock(), Save parameters, Release shutdown mutex - px4_shutdown_unlock(). The confusing part to me is the implementation of px4_shutdown_lock() and px4_shutdown_unlock(). Both functions wait for the mutex and release it immediately, so the actual param saving is not done with the mutex in this case. My question is how does this work?

nodes.label: Post by JulianOes explaining the shutdown lock mechanism
nodes.content: The mutex is used to access shutdown_lock_counter, basically a semaphore that holds the state whether reboot should be prevented or not. I assume that’s because there could be multiple writers, each of them bumping shutdown_lock_counter by one, and decreasing it again when they are done.

nodes.label: Reboot Prevention Mechanism
nodes.content: A software mechanism designed to prevent system reboots or shutdowns during critical operations like saving parameters.

nodes.label: Saving Parameters
nodes.content: The action of writing current system parameters to persistent storage.

nodes.label: px4_shutdown_lock()
nodes.content: A function that increments a counter to signal that a critical operation has started, preventing a system shutdown.

nodes.label: px4_shutdown_unlock()
nodes.content: A function that decrements a counter to signal that a critical operation has ended, allowing a system shutdown if the counter is zero.

nodes.label: shutdown_lock_counter
nodes.content: A counter variable that acts as a semaphore to track the number of active locks preventing system shutdown.

nodes.label: shutdown_mutex
nodes.content: A mutex used to ensure thread-safe access to the shutdown_lock_counter.

nodes.label: Mutex protects a counter acting as a semaphore
nodes.content: The shutdown_mutex is not meant to lock the entire parameter saving operation. Instead, it provides safe, atomic access to the shutdown_lock_counter. This counter functions as a semaphore, indicating whether a reboot is permitted. This allows multiple components to independently request a shutdown lockout.

nodes.label: Post by DeepSOIC: Initial Problem Report
nodes.content: Reports that after flashing the PX4 bootloader to a Kakute H7 mini v1.3, the board shows no signs of life (solid green LED) and is not detected as a USB device. Various bootloader versions were tried with the same result. Flashing Betaflight works correctly.

nodes.content: The user expresses confusion about why the pre-built bootloaders failed and shares a hypothesis that the bootloader was crashing while trying to log to an incorrectly formatted onboard blackbox flash chip.

nodes.content: Another user reports having no issues flashing the PX4 bootloader on the same hardware (Kakute H7 mini v1.3) using either dfu-util or STM32CubeProgrammer.

nodes.label: Issue Connecting Teraranger Evo 60m Tower to Pixhawk 6C / Cube Orange with PX4
nodes.content: A user is facing an issue connecting a Teraranger Evo 60m Tower sensor to a Pixhawk 6C or Cube Orange flight controller running PX4, due to a communication protocol mismatch (UART vs. I2C).

nodes.label: Post by James_lim detailing the connection issue
nodes.content:
Hello, I have encountered an issue while connecting Teraranger Evo 60m Tower to Pixhawk 6C / Cube Orange with PX4.

I’m trying to connect the Teraranger Evo 60m Tower to a Pixhawk 6C or Cube Orange running PX4 Autopilot but have encountered an issue.

From what I understand, PX4 only supports Teraranger sensors over I2C. However, the Teraranger Evo 60m Tower only provides a UART pinout in its datasheet, with no direct I2C support.

My Questions:

  1. Has anyone successfully connected the Teraranger Evo 60m Tower to PX4?
  2. Would I need a UART-to-I2C converter to make it compatible with PX4?
  3. Is there an alternative way to integrate this sensor with PX4, or is it simply unsupported?

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

nodes.label: Sensor Integration Protocol Mismatch

nodes.label: Post by rroche: Suggestion to check dmesg

nodes.label: Throttle smoothning in the mixer module or dshot output
nodes.content: A user investigates why the DSHOT throttle output is a constant value while the corresponding 'actuators_motors' topic shows a sinusoidal signal. The issue was eventually traced to smoothing being performed by the ESC and a faulty measurement setup.

nodes.label: Post by Motonaut describing throttle signal discrepancy
nodes.content: A user reports a problem where the throttle value on the DSHOT pins, measured with a logic analyzer, does not match the value published on the 'actuators_motors' topic. The DSHOT output is constant, while the topic value is sinusoidal, suggesting the signal is being low-passed somewhere.

nodes.label: Post by owen487: Clarification and Code Sharing
nodes.content: Clarifies that 'position' means orientation, not location. The core issue is creating a custom UAVCAN message for this data, as standard messages for accelerometer/gyro rates are unsuitable. Shares C++ code for the custom publisher and subscriber.

nodes.content: Suggests publishing to the 'vehicle_attitude' uORB topic instead of 'sensor_attitude' for filtered attitude data. Also proposes creating a new custom uORB topic if the only goal is logging.

nodes.label: Post by owen487: Clarifying Multi-instance Direction
nodes.content: Clarifies the problem is the reverse: publishing from multiple uORB topic instances on a CANnode to a single DroneCAN message, which is not covered by the provided PR.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl: Identifying Unsupported Feature
nodes.content: Explains that publishing from multiple uORB instances to a single DroneCAN topic is not currently supported in PX4, as the publisher class defaults to the first uORB instance.

nodes.label: Post by dakejahl: Explaining the ESCStatus Mechanism

nodes.content: Understands the 'trick' used by EscStatus. The solution is to modify the IMU driver to publish data from all IMUs into an array within a single custom uORB message, which can then be broadcast over DroneCAN.

Hello everyone,

I have been diving into the inner workings of PX4, specifically the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF2), and I’m trying to understand the reasoning behind certain design choices regarding quaternion correction and observation models.

From my understanding, the quaternion correction in EKF2 seems to be a fundamental part of the orientation estimation process, but I’m curious about a few aspects related to it:

  1. Quaternion Correction and EKF2: The quaternion correction in EKF2 appears to be well integrated for handling orientation, which is crucial for accurate state estimation. However, it seems that there is a more complex handling of observations beyond just correcting for orientation. Given that orientation estimation via quaternion correction is already non-trivial, when the observation models themselves appear relatively simple?

  2. Usage of Multiple Observations in EKF2: In the context of state estimation, how exactly are these body velocity and other observations incorporated into the filter? I understand that these observations help to refine the system’s state estimates, but how does the EKF leverage the multiple measurements in a way that improves its overall performance?

I’ve gone through the available documentation and slides, but I feel that certain implementation details aren’t fully covered. Any tips or guidance on this, especially with regard to how observations are processed in the EKF2 implementation and the rationale behind using multiple observations for specific state variables, would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks in advance for your insights!

nodes.label: Post by viswans2132 describing the initial problem
nodes.content: Describes the setup (Quadrotor, Pixhawk, ROS Humble, PX4, MicroXRCEAgent) and the core issue: on real hardware, `thrust_body` values from a `VehicleAttitudeSetpoint` ROS message appear in the quaternion field of the `ATTITUDE_TARGET` MAVLink message, causing the drone to disarm. This behavior differs from the SITL/Gazebo simulation.

nodes.label: Post by mylongword suggesting potential causes
nodes.content: Suggests potential causes including coordinate system differences (FLU vs. FRD) and conflicts in the `mc_att_control` module.

nodes.label: Post by viswans2132 refuting coordinate system issue

nodes.label: Post by mylongword questioning the PID script's logic
nodes.content: Points out a potential flaw in the PID script where a small angle assumption is used to calculate quaternions from acceleration values, which are not angles.

nodes.label: Post by viswans2132 acknowledging but dismissing the script logic issue
nodes.content: Acknowledges the point about the quaternion calculation but believes it's unrelated to the primary issue of data mis-mapping, as the values are clipped and the resulting quaternions are reasonable.

nodes.label: Post by viswans2132 announcing the solution
nodes.content: States that the issue is fixed. The problem was an outdated version of MicroXRCEAgent. Reinstalling the newest version resolved the data mapping conflict.

nodes.label: Post by mylongword about skewed-rotor instability
nodes.content: I had supposed yes, because the omnicopter flies. But is this just a special case? On testing a 6-rotor model in SITL gazebo, I have experimented with parameters without curing instability. 2 rotors are aligned to lift vertically. The model takes off and climbs to a 10m altitude target, but then attitude instability sets in, resulting in total instability. Some additional unsatisfactory behaviour during the climb to 10m: 2 rotors are correcting for motor torque that should be nearly cancelled by vehicle symmetry. The load is very badly distributed over the rotors: The 2 vertical-lift rotors do nearly all the lifting while another 2 rotors don’t spin until instability sets in. Any suggestions? Otherwise is it time for me to begin to study the code with the intention of writing my own simpler controller to handle 6-degree-of-freedom capability?

Connection closed by client.

I have also tried adding Eigen library to calculate the inverse, but the issue persists. It looks like a memory limitation.

  1. Is there any parameter that constraints the size of the matrix for inverse calculation?
  2. How can I compute the inverse/pseudo-inverse of high-dimensional matrix?

Any help would be much appreciated!

nodes.label: Flight Mode Unknown 1:655360 and Unknown 129:655360
nodes.content: A user experiences 'Flight Mode Unknown' errors with codes 1:655360 and 129:655360 while running PX4 in SITL.

nodes.label: Post by melc reporting the issue
nodes.content: Was running PX4 in SITL and encountered these mid-flight and after disarming. It has never happened since so it’s not a problem for now but just curious what could be the cause of it. Seems that it might be the enum for flight mode?

nodes.label: Post by melc specifying PX4 version
nodes.content: Thanks for the reply, it is a fork of v1.15. Maybe it’s an added number from a mixture of modes? Not too sure about it

nodes.label: Post by melc identifying potential cause
nodes.content: Are you building on top of v1.15 and above? I suspect it might be the new position slow mode introduced in v1.15. Old versions of QGC may not register this mode and display that unknown code instead.

nodes.label: Post by Bunny confirming the issue
nodes.content: I still see the issue with QGC v4.4.4. I am using v1.15. This specifically happens with Position Slow mode.

nodes.label: Post by JulianOes explaining the root cause and solution
nodes.content: Ok, I’ve found the issue. Back when QGC v4.4.x was initially developed, the standard modes MAVLink spec was still marked as “work in progress” and therefore it was only enabled for developer/daily builds but not for release. ... I will update MAVLink and get this into v4.4.5.

nodes.label: Post by JulianOes announcing the fix
nodes.content: Try QGC v4.4.5. It should work now.

graphs.title: Offboard no signal for physical drone

nodes.label: Offboard no signal for physical drone
nodes.content: A thread discussing the issue of 'offboard no signal' when trying to control a physical drone with a companion computer, which works in simulation but not in reality.

nodes.label: Post by Dobryng describing the problem
nodes.content: I am trying to offboard a quadcopter using a companion computer; jetson orin nx, and pixhawk 6c. I am using ros2 humble, using px4_ros_com pkg and the microagent to run the uORB topic for the drone. I can run gazebo sim with the drone proceeding to offboard, but when i want to offboard the physical drone, my QGC kept telling me offboard no signal. I am connecting my pixhawk 6c to the jetson via UART connection, i was manage to make the connection between px4 and microagent. When i try doing offboard, there isn’t any signal.

nodes.label: Post by alan asking for a solution
nodes.content: Hello，did you find solution？ I met the same problem.

nodes.label: Post by Dobryng providing the solution
nodes.content: Since the pixhawk 6c isn’t a reliable IMU, the drone wont even offboard. So you need to pub the odom topic from your VIO to the visual vehicle odom in the microagent. Then you have make sure the data matches if not it wont work. What that means is that when you pub the VIO into the visual vehicle odom, the x y z and q must match. You will need to keep checking and adjusting base on what transform frame you use. If all things go well, you should be able to offboard.

nodes.label: Post by owen487

I recently made a post asking what is actually supposed to be displayed when using CANnodes on the can bus. Since then I have figured out what I’m supposed to be seeing, and have discovered there is something wrong, whether it be me or PX4 (or maybe something else?)

Note: All of this is using QGC, Pixhawk 6, Ark CANnode

When I plug in my CANnodes, I seem to get only some of the information that I should. I can see the the nodes pop up in the parameters tab with their node ID’s, however when using `uavcan status` I get no sign of life. I also found (not surprisingly) that anything plugged into the nodes, an air-speed sensor for example, would also not show up anywhere. However, when I enter things such as `uavcan param list 124` it will display the relevant information as if an active node was there.

I’m not really sure whats going on and any help would be great. I don’t think the problem is the nodes themselves but if you think there is a reason why it would be do share

nodes.label: Post by AWilkins_Ascend with recommendations

This is in the eye of the beholder. I am not going to say what is the best, but your options are
Ark Electronics
ModalAI
Cubepilot
Holybro
3DR
If you buy all the components you need from the same spot you increase the likelihood of compatibility. You CAN mix and match, but if you are worried about compatibility then dont as manufacturers test their components together more often.
Should you use docker if you use linux: depends on your use case. if you do then whatever application you write is more portable from system to system and you dont have to worry about onboard compatibility issues. We use docker a lot…so short answer is yes

graphs.title: Issue with Battery Status in PX4

nodes.label: Issue with Battery Status in PX4
nodes.content: A user is experiencing an issue where sending battery status from a ROS node to QGroundControl via MAVLink causes a low battery failsafe (RTL) upon takeoff, despite the battery percentage displaying correctly. The core issues are an incorrect 'time_remaining' value (1s) and an incorrect battery ID (255) being reported.

nodes.label: Initial Problem Report by manudelu
nodes.content: Describes the initial problem: sending BATTERY_STATUS from a ROS node causes a low battery failsafe in PX4. Notes that QGC shows 'time_remaining' as 1s and battery ID as 255.

nodes.label: Analysis by sfuhrer
nodes.content: Analyzes the flight log and identifies the 'battery_low_remaining_time' failsafe is triggered because the time remaining is 0. Suspects a bug in the UavcanBatteryBridge and suggests updating PX4 or modifying the code.

nodes.label: Further Investigation by moritzNeo
nodes.content: Reports the same problem persists on newer firmware. Suspects a bug in the BATTERY_STATUS MAVLink stream where a uint8 underflow causes the battery ID to flip from 0 to 255 and a max() function incorrectly sets time_remaining to 1s.

nodes.label: Proposed Code Fix by moritzNeo
nodes.content: Provides a code snippet to modify the BATTERY_STATUS stream, fixing the ID mapping and removing the `max(time, 1)` logic. This resolves the 1s time remaining issue in MAVLink Inspector.

nodes.label: Workaround by moritzNeo
nodes.content: Reports that despite the code fix, the failsafe flag is still triggered internally. Proposes a workaround by modifying 'failsafe.cpp' to permanently disable the 'battery_low_remaining_time' failsafe action.

nodes.label: Post by anaam-wingxpand
nodes.content: When UAVCAN_BITRATE = 115200, the flight controller will hard fault when trying to run uavcan and get stuck in a bootloop. nodes.content: User Alp_Ucan suggests two methods. The first is a flexible custom approach involving creating a uORB topic and a new MAVLink stream. nodes.label: Post by Gman: Clarification of Hardware and Protocol
nodes.content: Gman clarifies they are using FEETECH STS bus servos with a URT-1 board, which do not use PWM. They require specific serial commands, which they demonstrate successfully sending from a desktop using a Python script with pyserial. They confirm that a custom module seems necessary.

nodes.label: Post by Alp_Ucan: Custom Driver Recommendation
nodes.content: Alp_Ucan confirms that a custom PX4 driver/module is the correct approach since the servo board requires specific commands, not MAVLink messages. They recommend using an existing UART driver like 'lightware_sf45_serial' as a template. An alternative solution using a companion computer (SBC) with MAVSDK is also proposed.

nodes.label: LiDAR Lite v3 with PX4 v1.15
nodes.content: A thread discussing issues and workarounds for using LiDAR Lite v3 with PX4 firmware versions 1.14 and 1.15.

nodes.label: Post by Luke_Connolly
nodes.content:
For anyone using a LiDAR Lite v3 with the Pixhawk flight controllers and using the firmware version 1.14 or 1.15, the drivers are not present with them, so the LiDAR won’t work either with I2C or PWM. I figured this out after days of troubleshooting.

How I got it to work was I reset the firmware back to v1.13, which with absolutely no changes, the LiDAR works. Once connected and working, I used QGC to update the firmware back to v1.15. However, this brings about the error “crash dumps present on sd px4”, which prevents arming.

How I then got around this was by changing the parameter “COM_ARM_HFLT_CHK” to disabled, allowing me to arm.

I have not tried using cmake to create the firmware v1.15 myself, making sure the driver is present under “src/drivers/distance_sensor/ll40ls” and “/ll40ls_pwm” folder, if anyone wants to give that a try and upload the resulting firmware here would be great.

nodes.label: Post by Ejemyr describing the initial problem
nodes.content: A user successfully implemented position control for a quadcopter in simulation using v1.15 flight modes and TrajectorySetpoints via a C++ node. However, when switching to a fixed-wing aircraft, the vehicle does not respond to the setpoints and turns left. The user questions if this method is supported for fixed-wing.

nodes.label: Post by Jaeyoung-Lim pointing out NAN usage
nodes.content: Suggests that the problem might be that the user has enabled acceleration and velocity setpoints but is sending NAN values for them.

nodes.label: Post by ahmad.zain detailing the solution
nodes.content: Discovered that the solution was to explicitly send NAN for the velocity field in the TrajectorySetpoint message, while sending zeros caused the issue. This is due to a check `Vector3f(trajectory_setpoint.velocity).isAllFinite()` in `FixedwingPositionControl.cpp` that, if it returns true (e.g., for zeros), sets a velocity setpoint that conflicts with the position target.

nodes.label: Post by Jaeyoung-Lim clarifying controller intent
nodes.content: Explains that sending both position and velocity together is intended for path following, where the guidance controller will follow the path using the closest point and tangent.

It is a small 250 frame and the cube is attached to small dampeners. I have tried multiple things to resolve this so my question is simply if any one ever experienced this and what could be the issue? I have tried multiple types of settings, different firmware versions, different dampeners, different PIDs, different filters (cutoff frequencies), different props, diffrent communication methods to the ESC etc. The results are always the same even though different versions of it. So instead of discussing the specifics of the rig and testing any new other thing I am looking for what could be the root cause of such oscillations. 1. Can a bad ESC-communication/connection cause this? Have tried oneshot and PWM400 and different firmware and versions on the ESC and also different units of the ESC (SpeedyBee BLS 60A 4-1 ESC). 2. Can bad electrical behaviour case this? Could connections and drops in power supply cause such an issue? Could that cause the OUTPUT to look like this? 3. Can a too responsive PID cause this? 4. nodes.content:
Hi!
I’m struggling since some time troubleshooting two issues what I have with my drone. Here is a log of the last test flight: https://review.px4.io/plot_app?log=91d7d73d-4546-4c54-a297-62d356249960

The antenna is 10 cm away from motor cables and 2 cm away from the battery (DC current shouldn’t be a big issue I assume?). This telemetry unit is recommended by the PX4 docs so I thought it should work without issues. I also didn’t change any GPS0_X / MAV0_X settings (it’s connected to GPS0).

For completeness I also attached a list of all parameters that are marked as “modified” in QGC.

nodes.label: Post by diana_diaz: Initial Question
nodes.content: I was wondering if it will be possible to control a RC Switch or the Kill Switch which I use to give enable the engine ignition and kill the engine, with some command from a USB Joystick which is connected to QGroundControl?

nodes.label: Post by dotanAtTrim: Suggests Custom Actions
nodes.content: You could use QGC’s Custom Mavlink Action and assign a Joystick button to that. ... last week I tried assigning a custom action to a Joystick button and could find my custom function in the drop-down menu ... It might be a bug or something on my end.

nodes.label: Post by dotanAtTrim: Recommends MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR for PX4
nodes.content: The structure of the JSON file remains the same between PX4 and Ardupilot, you only need to make sure to use Mavlink commands that are supported by PX4. It’s working for me using PX4. Command I use is MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR (187). I don’t see references to MAV_CMD_DO_SET_RELAY and MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO in PX4 source code.

nodes.label: Post by sfuhrer: Suggests COM_PREARM_MODE
nodes.content: You can make them work before arming through COM_PREARM_MODE. If you want more automation in the ICE control you can check out the ongoing work of adding a ICE module.

nodes.label: Post by diana_diaz: Solution Found
nodes.content: I have it now working. I was using 1.14.3 when I tested, now I use 1.15.2 as firmware and it works. In the Actuator section I selected Peripheral via Actuator Set 2 for channel two and assigned it to AUX2. Now my buttons also are steering the servos.

nodes.label: Crash after loss of GPS
nodes.content: A thread discussing a drone crash caused by GPS loss during autonomous flight, where the drone descended without stopping its horizontal movement. The discussion explores optical flow sensors as a potential solution.

nodes.label: Post by generalauto describing the crash
nodes.content: My hexarotor drone was flying in an autonomous mode while being controlled by an onboard companion computer. The logs then indicate it lost its GPS signal which triggered the failsafe and since it didn’t have a RC connected a descent was initiated. This is all good, only it was travelling at about 5m/s horizontally at the time, and it didn’t reduce horizontal speed during descent, so it hit the ground on an angle. Obviously this isn’t desirable so I was wondering if this is the expected behaviour, and if it is then would a PX4FLOW allow the drone to hold its position during a descent in this failsafe situation? edit: just realised the PX4FLOW is discontinued, maybe there is another optical flow device that will allow the drone to descend vertically in failsafe mode?

nodes.label: Post by dirksavage88 suggesting Ark Flow
nodes.content: I would not rely on PX4FLOW as it can be inaccurate with the rangefinder on board. The Ark Flow is the more modern solution to what you are looking for.

nodes.label: Post by generalauto suggesting Holybro H-Flow
nodes.content: Thanks for your reply. I’m hoping for something a little more cost effective. Holybro have just brought out something they call H-Flow which looks good and uses the same rangefinder chip, DroneCAN, is half the price, and has what looks like an upgraded optical flow chip. I’m just waiting for confirmation from holybro that it doesn’t require rolling back the PX4 version to 1.13.3 like their PWM3901 optical flow sensor does.

nodes.label: Post by Argas on PX4 time stamping and communication
nodes.content:
I am looking at PX4 and I have a couple questions on how time stamping works and approaches to communication to external computer if you want to use the IMU information for state estimation or control.

  1. Do any flight controllers use native USB 2.0 HID transfer vs a USB2Serial bridge?

  2. What is the correct approach to get accurate time information with respect to computer time of MU messages?

USB 2.0 communication is always controlled by the host which means best case scenario is around 1MS update rate using HID controller at full speed. If a different transfer type is used there is potentially unbounded latency.

Has this issue been investigated/addressed? How is it solved?

nodes.label: Post by dronesalot on port naming conventions
nodes.content:
I recognize that PX4 has had a lot of influence from the pixhawk type hardware that had ports like TELEM1, GPS2 and so on. With the addition of many low cost flight boards, this naming convention adds a lot of restriction and complexity.

Is it feasible to produce a naming convention for each board that matches its peripherals? My matek for example has 7 different serial ports, and being able to provision a port as serial 4 is far more intuitive than poking around to determine that RX4/TX4 are actually telem1.

Not certain exactly how to do this. I’ve seen some of the settings, but it isn’t clear what other items would be required to make it work seamlessly in QGroundControl or if this is even possible.

Why does acceleration control in offboard mode need velocity estimate?

nodes.label: Why does acceleration control in offboard mode need velocity estimate?
nodes.content: A thread discussing the requirement of a velocity estimate for acceleration control in PX4's offboard mode, especially in GPS-denied environments.

nodes.label: Post by ra1nyu: Initial problem description
nodes.content: User ra1nyu describes an issue where offboard acceleration control requires a velocity estimate, which is unavailable in their GPS-denied environment. They are using PX4 v1.15.0 and want to control z-velocity and xy-acceleration. They propose a code change in `offboardCheck.cpp` that works in SITL and question the necessity of the original check.

nodes.label: Post by Benja: Explanation of controller logic
nodes.content: User Benja explains that the OffboardControlMode flags are for feasibility checks in the commander, not the controller itself. The controller uses the TrajectorySetpoint message fields to decide which controller to run. Benja agrees the velocity check for acceleration seems unnecessary.

nodes.label: Post by ra1nyu: Follow-up experiment and idea
nodes.content: User ra1nyu confirms understanding the feasibility checks. They report that disabling the acceleration flag in the control mode message causes the multicopter position control module to be disabled, leading to a crash. This justifies keeping the flag enabled.

nodes.label: Post by MaEtUgR: Pull Request with a fix
nodes.content: User MaEtUgR creates a pull request (#24076) based on the discussion, proposing a fix to allow offboard acceleration control with only an attitude estimate, removing the dependency on a horizontal velocity estimate.

Hello everyone, I am working on testing model-based design control strategies in Simulink and then test them in px4_sitl and px4_hitl with Gazebo-Classic through OFFBOARD flight mode. In the setpoint message each field is populated, namely timestamp, frame_id, etc and I can see the topic correctly published in /mavros/setpoint_accel/accel. The environment is an Ubuntu Linux machine with version 20.04 and ROS Noetic. Mavros runs on board the RPi and the communication to the FCU is done through USB to TELEM2.

Thanks,
Elia

nodes.content: I’m developing a module for PX4. I have everything working on Linux/Posix, but I can’t get it to link on NuttX. It doesn’t find the symbols from the NuttX libraries that I’m using. I see the correct .a file from NuttX submitted on the compiler line, and I see the symbols in that .a file with nm. nodes.label: Post by henrihein providing the solution

graphs.title: Termination mode activation dangerous

nodes.label: Termination mode activation dangerous
nodes.content: A thread discussing the dangerous and unexpected activation of termination mode in PX4.

nodes.label: Post by javiAldazabal
nodes.content:
Hi there,
Using Cube Orange PX4 v1.14.3.
I recently detected in some flights that, when switching to offboard mode, aircraft enters termination mode. This happened in position mode when switching on ground to offboard. Also when switching to offboard on air (but thank goodness aircraft was on a rope).
But the worst thing is that this happened on ground once without offboard change.
After reviewing all flights, I detected that the pattern was that local position invalid failsafe flags were triggered. And the common fact in all of them was that in logging dropouts DELTA_1 was high (between 1000ms and 1700ms).
I understand that not having msgs for that interval makes PX4 to activate Termination mode. I have disabled the “high_rate & raw_FIFO_IMU_accel” in SDLOG_PROFILE to avoid this problem with the dropouts and delta.
However, it looks very strange that this mode is enabled due to excess of msgs, instead of reducing (or disabling) the msgs logging.
I find this issue very risky, what is your opinion about this?
Thanks in advance

graphs.title: Help Needed with PX4 Flight Control Issues
How to obtain relative position between two RTK GNSS receivers?

nodes.label: How to obtain relative position between two RTK GNSS receivers?
nodes.content: A thread discussing the method to calculate the relative position between two RTK GNSS receivers mounted on a UAV and a UGV.

nodes.label: Post by psvs
nodes.content: I have a UAV and UGV set up, each containing Ardusimple RTK GNSS receivers. Is there a way to get the relative position between them? Specification of GNSS receivers: ZED-F9P-02B.

nodes.label: Post by RP80
nodes.content:
You need to more clearly say what you want to achieve. Where do you need the relative position? In the UAV controller? In the UGV controller? In the base station computer? All 3? What type of data link do you have between the vehicles, if any. What type of data link between the vehicles and the base station, if any? What level of programming customisation is feasible in your setup?

The GNSS receivers can’t calculate their position relative to each other, only relative to the satellites and the earth. You will have to calculate the difference between the two positions. Since you have a UAV your calc may have to consider altitude also.

To calculate the relative position you need to transmit both positions so they are available to whatever controller runs the part of your code that does the calc.

If both vehicles need the difference then you have to decide if they should both calculate it independently or if one should do it and then transmit the result.

Final note the uncertainty will be high, 2x the error in the measurements which might be same order of magnitude as the position difference.

I realise that’s not a “how to” type answer but hopefully helpful.

nodes.label: Initial post describing oscillations and noise
nodes.content: I have a customized 770mm quadrotor. I believe that the rate tuning is ok. The pitch step response in the manual flight mode looks good. However, the acceleration in position mode is really noisy and the flight performance has quick oscillations. The only thing I observe is that the Z velocity is not well-tuned. Will that Z velocity affect the performance of X and Y axis?

nodes.label: Post suggesting Autotune and other factors
nodes.content: Have you tried to Autotune you UAV? Or try to find the right flightspeed. Wind can be a factor. But most likely it is the leveling or autoune.

nodes.label: Post confirming the solution
nodes.content: Hi, Thank you for replying. I have fixed it by improving the vibration isolation. The position mode amplified the noise level. The noise may come from my payload. I also tried autotune. It sets a high attitude gain which is interesting. My original PID is also good.

nodes.label: How to access PX4 parameters in offboard mode

nodes.label: Post by Giorgio-P98
nodes.content: Suggests three solutions: using telemetry radios with QGC, connecting the debug port to the Jetson to run QGC locally, or loading a pre-configured parameters file. Warns against changing parameters during flight.

nodes.label: Post by serkan
nodes.content: Asks if the 'ParameterSetValueRequest' uORB message can be used to set parameters.

nodes.label: Post by Halil
nodes.content: States that changing parameters is not possible with ROS2 currently, but was possible with MAVROS. Provides a working Python script using pymavlink to change parameters over MAVLink.

nodes.label: Post by Giorgio-P98
nodes.content: Confirms parameters cannot be set via ROS2 topics and recommends the pymavlink script or using QGC for its descriptive API.

nodes.label: Post by hamishwillee
nodes.content: Advises caution when changing parameters from a companion computer. Suggests MAVSDK as a method and confirms that writing directly to the 'ParameterSetValueRequest' uORB topic in ROS2 is a likely approach.

nodes.label: Post by hamishwillee
nodes.content: Summarizes the problem as a connectivity issue for QGC. Recommends telemetry radios or using MAVLink-Router to forward the MAVLink connection through the Jetson.

nodes.label: Post by terrymao886
nodes.content: Provides a link to a MAVSDK-Python example script for uploading parameters and shows a single parameter change example.
